Container.Name: hearth
Container.Overview:
Hearth: a household recipe box, meal planner and shopping list. Runs its database migrations on boot, then serves the app on port 3000 inside the container.
ON FIRST BOOT it writes a setup token to its log, the credential that creates the first account. Read it before you hand the address to anyone: docker logs hearth
Container.Requires: The `hearth` docker network, and hearth-db running on it.

Config.Name: Web port
Config.Description: Host port for the app. Point your reverse proxy at [unraid IP]:[this port].

Config.Name: Data directory
Config.Description: Holds the auth secret generated on first boot, and the first-boot setup token. MUST PERSIST: lose it and every member of the household is signed out.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: Replace CHANGE_ME with the POSTGRES_PASSWORD set on hearth-db. The host is the container name, resolved on the `hearth` network.

Config.Name: PUBLIC_URL
Config.Description: The address a browser uses, e.g. https://hearth.example.com. Scheme and host only. It is the auth base URL and trusted origin, and its https scheme is what marks session cookies Secure. Set it before anyone signs in.

Config.Name: TRUST_PROXY
Config.Description: Who may tell Hearth the real client address. Behind a reverse proxy, put that proxy's IP as unraid sees it (e.g. your firewall's LAN address for HAProxy on pfSense). A hop count (1) also works but trusts any machine that can reach the port. 0 trusts nobody: then every visitor shares one rate-limit bucket.

Config.Name: NODE_ENV
Config.Description: Leave as production. It makes logs JSON and makes the server refuse to start on the development secret published in the repository.

Config.Name: LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace or silent. Never silent without SMTP: invitation and verification links are then delivered only by being written to this log.

Config.Name: SMTP_HOST
Config.Description: Your mail relay. Blank: Hearth sends no mail and writes invitation and verification links to its log instead. Anyone who can read the log can then accept an invitation.

Config.Name: SMTP_SECURE
Config.Description: true for implicit TLS on 465, false for STARTTLS on 587.

Config.Name: SMTP_USER
Config.Description: Relay username. Set both this and SMTP_PASS, or neither.

Config.Name: SMTP_PASS
Config.Description: Relay password. Never written to a log line.

Config.Name: SMTP_FROM
Config.Description: The From address, on a domain your relay may send for.
